61709-revolt-on-the-earth-star.title: Revolt On The Earth Star
61709-revolt-on-the-earth-star.creator: Unknown
61709-revolt-on-the-earth-star.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Rod clung there, weak and shaken, almost crying his thankfulness. Immediately upon the cessation of exertion, however, the cold crept upon him and he finally regained sufficient control to examine his plight. His mittens were slick and wet; constantly he stretched numbing fingers for a new grasp upon the faithless ice as a treacherous film of water formed beneath them.

arxiv-1802-00094.title: Single Image Reflection Removal Using Deep Encoder-Decoder Network
arxiv-1802-00094.creator: Zhixiang Chi, Xiaolin Wu, Xiao Shu, Jinjin Gu
arxiv-1802-00094.description: Abstract Image of a scene captured through a piece of transparent and reflective material, such as glass, is often spoiled by a superimposed layer of reflection image. While separating the reflection from a familiar object in an image is mentally not difficult for humans, it is a challenging, ill-posed problem in computer vision.

arxiv-2205-14868.title: Emergence of cosmic space and its connection with thermodynamic principles
arxiv-2205-14868.creator: P. B. Krishna, Hassan Basari V. T, and Titus K Mathew
arxiv-2205-14868.description: Abstract The recent research on the connection between gravity and thermodynamics suggests that gravity could be an emergent phenomenon. Following this, Padmanabhan proposed a novel idea that the expansion of the universe can be interpreted as equivalent to the emergence of space with the progress of cosmic time.

arxiv-2206-06352.title: Null states from large superpositions of two-sided black holes
arxiv-2206-06352.creator: John Gardiner
arxiv-2206-06352.description: Abstract A standard insight of the AdS/CFT correspondence is that some aspects of the geometry of a bulk state are encoded in the entanglement structure of its dual boundary state. As entanglement is not a linear quantum observable, this means that geometry in a quantum theory of gravity should likewise not be a linear observable.

arxiv-2211-13682.title: A Null-space based Approach for a Safe and Effective Human-Robot Collaboration
arxiv-2211-13682.creator: Federico Benzi, Cristian Secchi
arxiv-2211-13682.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Federico Benzi, Cristian Secchi. During physical human robot collaboration, it is important to be able to implement a time-varying interactive behaviour while ensuring robust stability. Admittance control and passivity theory can be exploited for achieving these objectives. Nevertheless, when the admittance dynamics is time-varying, it can happen that, for ensuring a passive and stable behaviour, some spurious dissipative effects have to be introduced in the admittance dynamics. These effects are perceived by the user and degrade the collaborative performance.

arxiv-2405-06058.title: Large Language Models Show Human-like Social Desirability Biases in Survey Responses
arxiv-2405-06058.creator: Aadesh Salecha, Molly E. Ireland, Shashanka Subrahmanya, João Sedoc, Lyle H. Ungar, Johannes C. Eichstaedt
arxiv-2405-06058.description: Abstract Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are becoming more widely used to simulate human participants and so understanding their biases is important. We developed an experimental framework using Big Five personality surveys and uncovered a previously undetected social desirability bias in a wide range of LLMs.

arxiv-2501-06367.title: Resilient Endurance-Aware NVM-based PUF against Learning-based Attacks 4 Thanks: 4 This is the authors version of the extended abstract to appear at DATE 2025. This work is supported in part by the German Research Foundation (DFG) as part of the priority program “SPP 2377: Disruptive Memory Technolo
arxiv-2501-06367.creator: Hassan Nassar 1 , Ming-Liang Wei 2 , Chia-Lin Yang 2 , Jörg Henkel 1 , Kuan-Hsun Chen 3
arxiv-2501-06367.description: Abstract Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) based on Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) technology have emerged as a promising solution for secure authentication and cryptographic applications. By leveraging the multi-level cell (MLC) characteristic of NVMs, these PUFs can generate a wide range of unique responses, enhancing their resilience to machine learning (ML) modeling attacks.

arxiv-2504-01415.title: Systematic Literature Review of Automation and Artificial Intelligence in Usability Issue Detection Thanks: This work was supported by the Slovak Research and Development Agency under the Contracts no. APVV-23-0408, also by the Cultural and Educational Grant Agency of Slovak Republic (KEGA) under gr
arxiv-2504-01415.creator: Eduard Kuric, Peter Demcak, Matus Krajcovic, Jan Lang
arxiv-2504-01415.description: Abstract . Usability issues can hinder the effective use of software. Therefore, various techniques are deployed to diagnose and mitigate them. However, these techniques are costly and time-consuming, particularly in iterative design and development. A substantial body of research indicates that automation and artificial intelligence can enhance the process of obtaining usability insights.

arxiv-2504-11555.title: Sub-optimality of the Separation Principle for Quadratic Control from Bilinear Observations
arxiv-2504-11555.creator: Yahya Sattar, Sunmook Choi, Yassir Jedra, Maryam Fazel, Sarah Dean
arxiv-2504-11555.description: Abstract We consider the problem of controlling a linear dynamical system from bilinear observations with minimal quadratic cost. Despite the similarity of this problem to standard linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control, we show that when the observation model is bilinear, neither does the Separation Principle hold, nor is the optimal controller affine in the estimated state.

arxiv-2510-03793.title: Comment on ”Comment on Galina Weinstein’s article entitled ’Convergences and Divergences: Einstein Poincaré and Special Relativity’ ”
arxiv-2510-03793.creator: Galina Weinstein
arxiv-2510-03793.description: Abstract This paper provides a systematic response to the criticisms raised by Jean-Marc Ginoux in response to my review of his book on the history of relativity. Whereas my review was written in a strictly academic manner, Ginoux’s commentary intermingles mathematical objections with ad hominem insinuations about both Einstein and me.

arxiv-2602-04985.title: Parameterized Algorithms for the Drone Delivery Problem
arxiv-2602-04985.creator: Simon Bartlmae, Andreas Hene, Joshua Könen, Heiko Röglin
arxiv-2602-04985.description: Abstract Timely delivery and optimal routing remain fundamental challenges in the modern logistics industry. Building on prior work that considers single-package delivery across networks using multiple types of collaborative agents with restricted movement areas (e.g., drones or trucks), we examine the complexity of the problem under structural and operational constraints.

pmc-10685364.title: Exploring the effects and mechanism of peony pollen in treating benign prostatic hyperplasia
pmc-10685364.creator: Jun Mu, Junsheng Wu, Linrui Duan, Qian Yang, Xiaoting Liu, Huixin Bai, Yanhua Xie, Jie Li, Siwang Wang
pmc-10685364.description: Paeonia suffruticosa is widely cultivated globally due to its medicinal and ornamental value. Peony pollen (PP) is commonly used in Chinese folk medicine to make tea to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), but its molecular mechanism against BPH is yet to be comprehended.

pmc-10752125.title: To Cut or to Cast? An Evaluation of Demographics & Mortality in Operative, Conservative, and Failed- Conservative Management of Charcot Neuroarthropathy
pmc-10752125.creator: Michaela D. Pitcher, Jacob Staub, Mahad Muhammad, Kelly Dopke, Kirsten N. Mansfield, Christopher Stauch, Kaitlin L. Saloky, Erdi Ozdemir, Michael Aynardi
pmc-10752125.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Category:Midfoot/Forefoot; DiabetesIntroduction/Purpose:Charcot neuroarthropathy (CN) is a chronic, destructive disease linked with diabetic neuropathy that affects the bone structure, joints, and soft tissues of the foot. Treatment can vary from a conservative shoe modification to a below-the-knee amputation (BKA). With no evidence based guidelines for CN management, treatment regimens are physician specific and dependent on stage of CN, comorbidities, and ulceration status.

pmc-11387841.title: Domestic dogs as reservoirs for African trypanosomiasis in Mambwe district, eastern Zambia
pmc-11387841.creator: Malimba Lisulo, Boniface Namangala, Cornelius Mweempwa, Maxwell Banda, Herman Chambaro, Ladslav Moonga, Hayashida Kyoko, Sugimoto Chihiro, Kim Picozzi, Sutherland K Maciver, Ewan T MacLeod
pmc-11387841.description: The control of African trypanosomiasis (AT) in Eastern and Southern Africa, including Zambia, faces huge challenges due to the involvement of wild and domestic animal reservoirs. Free-roaming dogs in wildlife-populated and tsetse-infested villages of Zambia’s Mambwe district are exposed to infectious tsetse bites. Consuming fresh raw game meat and bones further exacerbates their risk of contracting AT.

pmc-12434382.title: Visual stimulus-evoked blood velocity responses in individual human posterior cerebral arteries measured with dynamic phase-contrast functional MR angiography
pmc-12434382.creator: Zhangxuan Hu, Sébastien Proulx, Grant A. Hartung, Daniel E. P. Gomez, Jingyuan E. Chen, Divya Varadarajan, Elif Gökçal, Saskia Bollmann, Can Ozan Tan, M. Edip Gurol, Jonathan R. Polimeni
pmc-12434382.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Functional MRI (fMRI) tracks brain activity through the associated hemodynamic changes via neurovascular coupling. Neurons communicate with the microvessels of the parenchyma to initiate a hemodynamic response, and these microvessels then communicate with upstream arterioles and arteries. The role of the larger feeding arteries—far upstream from the site of neuronal activity—in coordinating this response is incompletely understood, yet is important for the interpretation of fMRI.

pmc-12631189.title: Metabolic Reprogramming in Urological Tumors: New Perspectives from Tumor Metabolic Phenotypes to Therapeutic Targets
pmc-12631189.creator: Zhuohang Li, Lin Yang, Weijia Li, Wenxue Huang, Cunzhen Ma, Boyuan Sun, Xunguo Yang, Haoxiang Xu, Zhibiao Li, Jie Zhao, Bisheng Cheng, Peng Wu
pmc-12631189.description: Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer, enabling tumor cells to sustain growth, evade immune surveillance, and resist therapy. Urological tumors, including prostate, bladder, and renal cancers, exhibit distinct metabolic phenotypes driven by their unique tumor microenvironments and oncogenic pathways.

pmc-12632434.title: Ultrafast Intermolecular Dynamics of Nanoconfined Water in Swollen Lipid Cubic Mesophases
pmc-12632434.creator: Eva Zunzunegui‐Bru, Serena Rosa Alfarano, Patrick Züblin, Laura Baraldi, Hendrik Vondracek, Federica Piccirilli, Lisa Vaccari, Raffaele Mezzenga
pmc-12632434.description: Understanding the structure and dynamics of the hydrogen‐bond network of water in topologically distinct swollen lipidic mesophases, is fundamental for their application in biomedical, pharmaceutical, and food science fields. Here, a positive and non‐linear correlation between water hydrogen‐bond dynamics and interfacial water population is uncovered in inverse bicontinuous swollen mesophases across an extended temperature range (298–340 K).

pmc-12983808.title: Understanding barriers and facilitators of adherence to lifestyle changes in prediabetes: a qualitative study
pmc-12983808.creator: Ana Sofia Carvalho-Azevedo, Raquel Sebastián-Hernández, Manuela Abbate, Sergio Fresneda, María Arias-Fernández, Aina M Yañez, Miquel Bennasar-Veny, Cristina Moreno-Mulet
pmc-12983808.description: BackgroundHealth interventions for individuals with prediabetes are essential to prevent or delay progression to type 2 diabetes. Adherence to lifestyle modification is complex and influenced by social determinants that act as barriers or facilitators. Gender, social class, social support, and the patient–professional relationship may shape individuals’ capacity to adopt and maintain behavioural changes.

pmc-13207880.title: Does Depression Increase the Risk of Endometriosis? A Combined Population‑Based and Laboratory Study
pmc-13207880.creator: Yuru Wang, Zihan Zhu, Xu Jin, Zhaoyan Ding, Wen Zhong, Yueming Zhang, Songwei Feng, Ting Wu
pmc-13207880.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEndometriosis is a chronic, estrogen-dependent inflammatory disorder that causes substantial pain and infertility. Observational studies have reported higher rates of multiple psychiatric disorders among individuals with endometriosis; however, confounding and reverse causation limit causal interpretation.MethodsWe performed bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from European-ancestry populations to test causal relationships between genetic liability to depression, anxiety, insomnia, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and endometriosis.

pmc-13210422.title: Multi-Component 3D Bioprinted Platform with Sacrificial Matrix and Collagen-Based Bioinks for Skeletal Muscle Tissue Engineering
pmc-13210422.creator: Carmen Mª. Granados-Carrera, Francisco José Calero Castro, Victor M. Perez-Puyana, Mercedes Jiménez-Rosado, Jaime Navarrete-Damián, Fernando de la Portilla de Juan, Alberto Romero
pmc-13210422.description: The development of biomimetic and mechanically functional constructs remains a major challenge in skeletal muscle tissue engineering. In this study, we present a multi-component 3D bioprinted platform integrating a polycaprolactone (PCL) support for mechanical stimulation, a sacrificial gelatin (GE) matrix for controlled bioink deposition, and collagen-based bioinks laden with Rattus norvegicus L6 skeletal muscle cells.
